clue.text: Whimsical short joke on topless type of dancing

indicators.note: short means the word for joke loses its final letter

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke

indicators.note: topless means the dancing word loses its first letter, its top in a down entry

parts.note: exotic dancing is a kind of striptease

explanation.surface: A dancer's wry remark about topless dancing is fanciful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter and 'topless' the first, the top of a down entry; 'on' places one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: quixotic, after Don Quixote, describes idealistic, fanciful and impractical notions.

clue.text: Comedienne's lines collected by being husband-free

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; the comedienne is Tracey Ullman

indicators.note: the lines are gathered up inside the other piece
free of husband means the abbreviation H (husband) is removed

parts.note: a being is a human

explanation.surface: A comedy actress's material was gathered while she was single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband-free' drops H, the abbreviation for husband; 'Comedienne's' is 'comedienne is', so Tracey Ullman is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Ullman is a British comic actress famous for sketch shows in Britain and the US.

clue.text: Sort of mess that's put away when picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: food put away is eaten

explanation.surface: A kind of mess that gets eaten when it's served up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when picked up' means heard: EATEN said aloud gives ETON. Eton mess is a British pudding of strawberries, meringue and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess is a named British dessert, so the school's name is a sort of mess.

clue.text: Rest of school party, except the head

indicators.note: the head of the party word, its first letter, is dropped

parts.note: a fiesta is a festive party

explanation.surface: The rest of a school party, all but the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except the head' drops F from FIESTA to give IESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an afternoon nap is a form of rest.

clue.text: Time's up in two places — doesn't it fly!

indicators.note: the piece appears twice over, in two spots
in a down entry up means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: EST is Eastern Standard Time; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: An exclamation that time has run out in two places, and how it flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EST into TSE, and 'in two places' writes it twice. The surface plays on 'time flies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African fly, so the exclamation names an insect that flies.

clue.text: Single or, in the old top flight, double

parts.note: Division One (DIV I) was the old name for the top tier of English football
dual means double

explanation.surface: A question about whether a player was single or doubled up in the old top division.
explanation.walkthrough: English football's top flight was Division One until the Premier League began in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something single is individual, one on its own.

clue.text: Listen, you should be in somewhere magical — you should be in Australia!

indicators.note: the word for you is to be placed inside the place name

parts.note: Oz is the magical land of the Wizard of Oz
ye is old word for you

indicators.note: again the word for you is to be placed inside the place name

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia
ye is old word for you

explanation.surface: Someone tells another person they belong in a magical land, or else Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is both L. Frank Baum's magical land and slang for Australia. The answer is the town crier's call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry comes from Old French for 'hear ye', a court officer's call meaning listen.

clue.text: Refusal of nearly every other poem entered

indicators.note: the poem goes inside the selected letters
taking every other letter of the word nearly, starting from the first

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Nearly every other poem submitted was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every other' picks N, A, L from 'nearly', and 'entered' puts ODE inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a flat refusal to an offer in a negotiation is announced with this phrase.

clue.text: A bed for Madame Bovary in the dark

parts.note: un is French for a
lit is French for bed, as the French heroine of Flaubert would say

explanation.surface: Madame Bovary's bed sits in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Bovary signals French, so 'A' and 'bed' turn into UN and LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a place with no lamps burning is in darkness.

clue.text: Writer elected to cover mad cow disease

indicators.note: the elected word wraps round the disease abbreviation

parts.note: someone elected is in
BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy, is mad cow disease

explanation.surface: A journalist was voted in to report on the mad cow disease outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests a journalist on the story, but it is the definition; 'to cover' means wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House, is a famous writer.

clue.text: The old, old, old MP

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: A doddering, very old member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' is 'the' in an old form, YE; the next 'old' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Yeo is a former Conservative member of parliament, so an old MP.

clue.text: Cardinal keeping two central letters back for Grand Inquisitor

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read backwards
the number holds the letters inside it

parts.note: six is a cardinal number
N and M sit at the middle of the alphabet, spelt out EN and EM

explanation.surface: A cardinal holds back two letters to stand in for the Grand Inquisitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts EN EM inside SIX and 'back' turns SENEMIX round. 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman but is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Ximenes (Cisneros) led the Spanish Inquisition as its Grand Inquisitor.

clue.text: Spin doctor avoids precipitative fall-out with third world leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their first letters
the doctor is left out of the rain word

parts.note: drizzle is light rain falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A spin doctor sidesteps the fallout from a world crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin doctor' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Spin' is the definition and 'doctor' the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to twizzle is to twirl or spin round.

clue.text: Poor quality shelter encounters earth tremor

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter

indicators.note: a tremor shakes the earth, so its letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Shoddy shelter caught in an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tremor' shakes EARTH into HRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something tenth-rate is of very low, inferior quality.

clue.text: Extremely funny Conservative hairstyle gets brutal treatment

indicators.note: the letters are roughed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's hairdo is savagely mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets brutal treatment' rearranges C plus HAIRSTYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hilarious joke is described informally as screamingly funny.

clue.text: Code-breaker's mostly shrouded location?

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Alan Turing was the wartime code-breaker at Bletchley Park; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A code-breaker is kept mostly under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the final G from TURING.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city houses the famous Shroud, the linen cloth said to be Christ's burial wrap.

clue.text: Bucolic scene written about in hillbilly diaries

indicators.note: about means the hidden letters are read in reverse
the letters sit inside the words hillbilly diaries

explanation.surface: A rustic scene described in the journals of mountain folk.
explanation.walkthrough: LLYDI sits across 'hillbilly diaries' and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a peaceful, picturesque rural scene, often described in pastoral poetry.

clue.text: Kiss, promise, and then wonder what you're doing

parts.note: a kiss is written as X, a cross
to give your word is to promise
to puzzle is to wonder

explanation.surface: A romance: a kiss, a vow, then second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the solver, who is doing exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone reading the clue is busy solving one, which makes it a self-referential description.

clue.text: Repeated pattern lost in a top with no sleeves

indicators.note: a top with its sleeves cut off loses its outer parts, so the letters sit inside the phrase lost in a top

explanation.surface: A sleeveless top went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no sleeves' strips the outer letters L and P from the phrase, leaving its inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a musical phrase that recurs persistently throughout a piece.

clue.text: Pre-Roman sculpture of centaurs

indicators.note: sculpting reshapes material, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Ancient statuary depicting centaurs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscan civilisation of central Italy flourished before Rome rose to power.

clue.text: Immerse oneself in British articles

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Losing oneself in British newspaper features.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to take a bath or swim is to immerse yourself in water.

clue.text: From the sublime to the ridiculous. Diocese sacrifices and … Well, gets nothing in return

definitions.text: From the sublime to the ridiculous

indicators.note: the shortened name receives a further letter
the letter goes in, as something received in exchange
the diocese name gives up these words

parts.note: Bath and Wells is a Church of England diocese in Somerset
the words and and Well, taken out of the diocese name
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A church diocese gives things up and receives nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath and Wells loses 'and Well', leaving BATHS, and O goes inside. The definition describes a comic anticlimax.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an abrupt descent from an elevated tone to the trivial or absurd.

clue.text: Offensive remark by men about Alsop originally being a poor conductor

indicators.note: the insult goes round the letter

parts.note: an insult is an offensive remark

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the name

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: Men making an offensive remark about the orchestra conductor Marin Alsop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside INSULT. Alsop is a real conductor, which steers the solver towards music.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics sense: an insulating material stops heat or electricity passing through, so conducts poorly.

clue.text: Inuit's building where it belongs

indicators.note: building constructs something new from these letters

explanation.surface: The Inuit dwelling sits in its proper place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original or proper position.

clue.text: Pick and shovel initially put in office

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of shovel

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone into office

explanation.surface: Tools such as a pick and a shovel are stored in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick and shovel' looks like a tool pair, but 'Pick' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to select is to choose, the verb sense of pick.

clue.text: A beating which leaves a lasting impression?

definitions.meaning: a rhythmic drumming or tapping, as in a drum signal
inked skin art stays permanently on the body

explanation.surface: A thrashing that scars someone for life.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a drumbeat and a permanent inked design on skin.

clue.text: Poles involved in hard labours — might they be removed?

indicators.note: the poles go inside the labours word

parts.note: toils are hard labours
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish workers doing forced labour, at risk of being sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like nationality but means N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The throat glands are often taken out in childhood surgery, so may well be removed.

clue.text: T S Eliot's quirky figure of speech

indicators.note: quirky means odd, so the letters are oddly rearranged

parts.note: the poet's name gives the letters; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: An eccentric turn of phrase by the poet T S Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad', a rhetorical device.

clue.text: Volunteers on Times newspaper prepare for take-off?

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
X is the multiplication sign, times
the i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Volunteers working on the Times newspaper get ready to launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the paper but is the sign X; the i is a British daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft move slowly along the runway, called taxiing, before taking off.

clue.text: Go for flipping instruction to cycle

indicators.note: to cycle means a letter moves round from one end to the other

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to flip the page

explanation.surface: Choosing between a flip-and-turn instruction and a cycling one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cycle' moves the P of PTO to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to opt is to choose or decide in favour of something.

clue.text: Maize: the regularly cited beginning for American culture

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of these words
the beginning of cited is its first letter

explanation.surface: The setter Maize says corn is often cited as the root of American culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A, Z, T, E from 'Maize: the'. Maize is this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztec civilisation of Mexico was a Mesoamerican culture built on maize farming.

clue.text: African tribesman has ox slaughtered

indicators.note: slaughtered means destroyed, so these letters are broken up

explanation.surface: A tribesman has an ox butchered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Xhosa are a Bantu people of South Africa, so a member is an African tribesman.
